correctness.rationale: Independently establish the unrestricted theorem using the Apéry set at m. If a tuple fails, its total belongs to the Apéry set, and each partial sum does too: subtracting m from a partial sum in S would give the same possibility at the total. From zero through the total these are m strictly increasing elements, exhausting the m residue representatives. All but the first positive partial sum are decomposable, so there is only one generator other than m (at least one by cofiniteness). Write S=<m,a>, a>m and gcd(m,a)=1. If any tuple member uses a copy of m, subtraction succeeds directly. Otherwise all entries are positive multiples of a; a total containing m or more copies of a admits replacing m of them by a copies of m. The only remaining tuple is the all-a tuple, whose defective sum is the greatest of the residue-class gaps ja−m, 0≤j<m, and hence is Frobenius. This independently gives the same exact witness as the frozen zero-sum and gap-reflection route. Inspection also confirms that the supplied Kunz checker is bounded (multiplicities 3–7, coordinates 1–4, recorded 2344 cases); it was not executed and was not needed for the universal proof.
residual_risks: The definition requires all positive ordered tuples, allowing repeated entries; there is no conclusion for an all-distinct-tuples variant or arbitrary earlier hierarchy levels.

evidence: The prior extremal zero-sum fact controls only residues. The missing step is to show that a failure cannot survive any extra atom or any upward shift of an entry by m. value.rationale: The last proper level of an existing hierarchy is a natural uniform boundary, not an arbitrary finite slice. A simple invariant decides it for every multiplicity, and the theorem describes precisely which tuple fails and what gap it produces. This links hierarchy membership to an elementary generator test while explaining the entire extremal obstruction, beyond the previously exhibited examples or the all-semigroup endpoint.
residual_risks: The result does not classify any earlier tier uniformly, and the underlying cyclic and two-generator theory is standard.
